title: Tbilisi bus sign and the Georgian banquet
summary: Joe Wilder asks what the bus sign says, and the Georgian president's 22 toasts leave everyone drunk.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: When we were in Georgia, about the second place, we went to Tbilisi, it used to be called Tiflis (PHONETIC) in Georgia, and that's one of the Soviet Republics there. And we were riding on a bus going to the date every night and up in the front of the bus is a big sign in Russian. And Joe Wilder knew I could read Russian so Joe Wilder says, "What does that sign say?" I said, "Joe, I'm sorry you asked me that. You know where we are, Joe?" "Yeah, in Georgia." "It says, 'get in the back of the bus.'"

He says, "Oh, Jimmy, you dadblamed rascal." The president of Georgia had this big banquet for us and he said it was a Russian custom that he drinks 22 toasts in a row of big waterglasses of wine, everybody's got to empty them. And then he turns over the toast to somebody else. Well, that party is one of the funniest parties I ever went to because by the time everybody got through 22 glasses of wine, most people are pretty well bombed. And, you know, we had the CIA following us around, and newspaper reporters and people from Time and Life.
